findings.description: The EC2 instance's user_data script embeds a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMAAAKEY). User data is readable via the instance metadata service and is stored in Terraform state, so anyone with instance access or state access obtains long-lived AWS credentials.

SSH (port 22) is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's remote administration to brute-force and exploit attempts from the entire internet. SSH should be restricted to a trusted administrative CIDR or accessed via bastion/SSM.

HTTP (port 80) is open to 0.0.0.0/0. While public web traffic may be intended, this exposes the unhardened instance directly to the internet; combined with the open SSH rule it substantially widens attack surface.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a publicly routable IP, including instances that are not intended to be internet-facing. Combined with the permissive security group this directly exposes workloads.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to all instances launched in this subnet, enlarging the internet-accessible footprint even for internally oriented workloads.
The S3 bucket that stores VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, so log data is written unencrypted and can be read directly if the underlying storage or backups are accessed.

The flow-log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no bucket policy or ACL restriction is defined, leaving the bucket's public-access defaults unprotected against accidental or malicious public exposure of network telemetry.
The EBS volume is created without an encrypted = true setting, so data written to the disk is stored unencrypted and is recoverable from snapshots or physical media.
The EBS snapshot of the portal disk is created without encryption, so the snapshot content is stored unencrypted and can be copied or shared in that state.
